sources.quote: IBAC represents more than 43,000 property and casualty brokers nationally
sources.title: About IBAC - Insurance Brokers Association of Canada
sources.evidence: The Insurance Brokers Association of Canada (IBAC) is the national voice of over 43,000 Property and Casualty (P&C) insurance brokers, representing and advocating for the best interests of insurance brokers and consumers. IBAC has 11 Member Associations that collectively represent over 43,000 insurance brokers.

sources.quote: RIBO released Guidance 006 on online conduct on June 1, 2026, holding Ontario brokers to the same professional standard online as off
sources.title: Stay Professional, Even Online: New Social Media Guidance - RIBO - Registered Insurance Brokers of Ontario
sources.evidence: RIBO Guidance 006 addresses Online Conduct (Social Media and Review Manipulation) and was posted on June 1, 2026. The purpose of this guidance is to inform individual and firm licensees of RIBO's expectations regarding professional conduct for social media and the use of online review platforms, and it interprets existing Code of Conduct obligations in the context of licensees' online conduct. It also offers practical direction to Principal Brokers in updating their firm's Plan of Supervision.

sources.quote: Google prohibits descriptors that are not part of the real-world name
sources.title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: Your business name should reflect your business's real-world name, as used consistently on your storefront, website, stationery, and as known to customers. Including unnecessary information in your business name isn't permitted, and could result in the suspension of your Business Profile. Add additional details like address, service area, business hours, and category in the other sections of your business information.

sources.quote: 5 to 10 percent B2C, 2 to 5 percent B2B
sources.title: What is an average marketing budget for a small business?
sources.evidence: B2B companies should spend between 2 and 5% of their revenue on marketing, and for B2C companies, the proportion is often higher—between 5 and 10%. This is because B2C companies typically need to invest in more marketing channels to reach various customer segments.

sources.quote: Ontario's Financial Professionals Title Protection Rule has required a FSRA-approved credential since March 2022
sources.publisher: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA)
sources.title: Ontario strengthens consumer protection by regulating who can use Financial Planner and Financial Advisor titles | Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario
sources.evidence: The Financial Professionals Title Protection (FPTP) Rule came into effect when the Financial Professionals Title Protection Act, 2019 and related amendments were proclaimed into force on March 28, 2022. Under the FPTP Rule, individuals using the Financial Planner or Financial Advisor title will need to hold an approved credential from a FSRA-approved credentialing body.

sources.quote: New Brunswick's act took effect on January 1, 2026 with a transition period
sources.publisher: Financial and Consumer Services Commission of New Brunswick (FCNB)
sources.title: Financial Advisors and Financial Planners | New Brunswick Financial and Consumer Services Commission
sources.evidence: The Financial Advisors and Financial Planners Title Protection Act came into force on January 1, 2026. The transition periods – two years for financial advisors and four years for financial planners – give individuals time to comply with the framework. These periods apply to individuals using these titles without an approved credential on or before January 1, 2026.

sources.quote: with penalties reaching $1 million for an individual and $10 million for an organization
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: The maximum amount of an administrative monetary penalty (AMP) per violation for an individual is $1 million, and for a business it is $10 million.

sources.quote: since June 2025 competitors can bring such applications to the Competition Tribunal
sources.title: Private access to the Competition Tribunal
sources.evidence: Private access rights have been extended to cases involving deceptive marketing practices, and these changes come into force on June 20, 2025. Starting June 20, 2025, people can directly apply for permission to file an application against businesses under the deceptive marketing practices provisions of the Act. If you want to apply, you must first ask the Competition Tribunal for leave (permission).

sources.quote: The Insurance Bureau of Canada reported severe-weather insured losses above $2.4 billion in 2025, a top-ten year, after a record $9.4 billion in 2024
sources.title: Severe weather-related insured losses in Canada exceed $2.4 billion in 2025
sources.evidence: Insured damage caused by severe weather events exceeded $2.4 billion in 2025, according to Catastrophe Indices and Quantification Inc. (CatIQ). This makes 2025 the tenth costliest year on record for severe weather-related insured losses in Canada. In 2024, annual insured losses reached a staggering $9.4 billion.

sources.quote: as of July 1, 2026, most statutory accident benefits became optional on new policies, with medical, rehabilitation and attendant care still mandatory
sources.publisher: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA)
sources.title: Changes in Statutory Accident Benefits coverage in Ontario on July 1, 2026 | Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario
sources.evidence: Medical, rehabilitation and attendant care benefits are mandatory benefits for policies entered into on or after July 1, 2026. For policies entered into after July 1, 2026, all other accident benefits, like income replacement, caregiver, or housekeeping and home maintenance, are optional.
